nodes.label: ADR 0004: MQTT Broker — Eclipse Mosquitto
nodes.rationale: Personal scale needs no clustering; tiny footprint; per-device username/password auth with revocable credentials (supports US-DEV-004) and topic ACLs; ubiquitous, boring, easy to replace behind standard MQTT protocol if scale demands it.

nodes.label: ADR 0005: Interim Field-Data Entry on Web Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Android app (authoritative field-data surface) ships late in Phase 1; without any entry surface the backend can't be used end-to-end by the sole operator, so web ships interim entry forms calling the same API endpoints, time-boxed until Android ships.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005: interim field-data entry on web dashboard

nodes.label: ADR 0006: Radxa SBC as Always-On Deployment Host
nodes.rationale: Broker and API server must be reachable continuously including overnight during active incubation (availability-critical per nfr.md); a laptop that sleeps/closes/moves breaks both. Owner already runs a Radxa SBC full-time on the same LAN.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0006: radxa sbc as always-on deployment host

nodes.label: ADR 0007: apps/api Deployed via systemd, Not Docker
nodes.rationale: Dockerizing apps/api requires cross-building ARM64 for a pnpm monorepo with two workspace deps — more moving parts than needed. Radxa already has Node 22 natively; running as a plain Node process under systemd gives the same restart/boot guarantees without a build/registry step.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007: apps/api deployed via systemd, not docker
